verdict.rationale: Authenticator documents push sign-in with approve/deny (docs-24) and number matching (docs-22/35). Admins control availability: notifications only 'if allowed by your administrator', and community admins report enforcing Authenticator push only. Location context is evidenced only as hourly location sharing to enforce country-based access (docs-15), not as sign-in location shown in the push prompt. Missing for 10: documentation of sign-in location or app context displayed in push notifications, first-party admin docs on configuring and enforcing number matching and MFA policies, independent corroboration of the phishing-defense behavior.

support.subject: As an IT admin, push-based sign-in includes phishing defenses — number matching, location context, and admin-enforced MFA policies

citations.quote: Users can receive an MFA request on their mobile device, and approve or deny the sign-in attempt from their phone.
Tap or enter the corresponding number, then Approve.
You can set up notifications for your work or school account (if allowed by your administrator)
You'll need to share your location once every hour to ensure you're still within a country where you are allowed to access the resource.
Now the only authenticator app my company allows is Microsoft Authenticator using push notifications.
